solutionSql:
SELECT e.shipment_id
FROM shipment_events e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM invoices i WHERE i.shipment_id = e.shipment_id
)
UNION
SELECT i.shipment_id
FROM invoices i
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM shipment_events e WHERE e.shipment_id = i.shipment_id
)
ORDER BY shipment_id;

rules.howSolved: The UNION of the scan-without-invoice set and the invoice-without-scan set returns both kinds of mismatch.
Each side uses NOT EXISTS against the other table, so a shipment with both a scan and an invoice never appears.

ambiguities: 'Shipment' is taken from the id column of whichever table holds the row. A FULL JOIN of the two distinct id sets gives the same result on sample, nulls and boundary, and those datasets have no orphan rows.
notes: Sample returns 49 rows, nulls 85, boundary 37. A FULL JOIN cross-check gives 0 differences on all three datasets.
